title: Ericsson Canada and ÉTS Partner to Develop Scalable Variational Quantum Algorithms for Telecom Network Optimization - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Ericsson Canada and Montreal's ÉTS launched a Mitacs Accelerate-funded research project, led by Prof. Jacob Biamonte, applying dissipative-engineering methods to make variational quantum algorithms scale for telecom routing, scheduling and resource allocation. It is the second academic project of Ericsson's Montreal Quantum Research Hub (founded 2022), after work with Université de Sherbrooke.

insights.claim: Ericsson Canada and École de technologie supérieure (ÉTS) formed a research collaboration, funded through Mitacs Accelerate, to develop scalable variational quantum algorithms for dynamic routing, traffic scheduling and resource allocation in telecom networks.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Telecom incumbents are exploring quantum optimization at research stage; signals long-dated, low-cost optionality rather than near-term revenue.

insights.claim: ÉTS graduate students and postdocs will run algorithms on physical quantum hardware backends and evaluate them against classical telecom benchmarks.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Benchmarking against classical baselines will show whether quantum adds value for telecom optimization.

insights.claim: Variational quantum algorithms are seen as leading candidates for NISQ utility, but their combinatorial-optimization performance is often limited by barren plateaus and accumulated incoherent noise.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Key technical risk for near-term quantum optimization claims; temper expectations for NISQ commercial utility.
